Here is the number that should concern every executive this week: 91%.

That is the percentage of organizations that have adopted AI but have not fundamentally changed how they operate because of it. SAP's latest global research with Oxford Economics found that companies are already running AI across roughly 25% of business tasks — but only 9% have actually adapted their business around AI.

The difference matters more than it sounds. Most companies took their existing processes and added AI on top. Faster reports. Smarter search. Automated steps in workflows that were designed decades ago. That delivers incremental efficiency. It does not deliver competitive advantage.

The 9% that broke through did something structurally different. They rethought decision rights, redesigned data governance, changed how performance gets measured, and rebuilt operating models around what AI makes possible — not just what it can speed up.

As AI capabilities compound — autonomous agents, multimodal reasoning, real-time systems — the gap between these two groups will become the defining competitive divide across every industry.

The question for leadership teams is direct: Is your AI deployment changing how your organization makes decisions, or just accelerating the old way?
